items.title: Decoupling Semantics and Logic: A Training-Free Coarse-to-Fine Pipeline for Video Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Training-free coarse-to-fine video RAG pipeline decoupling semantic retrieval (BGE-M3 dense embedding) from logical reasoning (LLM-based A.I.R. agent). Uses modality decoupling, iterative cognitive reranking, and prompt sculpting for persona-constrained generation with chunk-level temporal grounding.

system.prefilter_rationale: Training-free video RAG pipeline with practical architectural patterns (semantic/logic decoupling, modality-aware retrieval, LLM-based reranking) directly applicable to production document intelligence and agentic workflows; addresses real constraints (hallucination, temporal grounding, persona adherence) relevant to Hermes-type systems.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly addresses RAG pipeline architecture with retrieval-augmentation patterns and agentic reasoning, but video-specific scope and training-free constraints limit applicability to text/document-centric production systems.
system.value_rationale: The coarse-to-fine decoupling pattern and iterative cognitive reranking architecture offer transferable design patterns for hybrid retrieval pipelines; chunk-level grounding and persona-constrained generation are relevant to document intelligence workflows, though video modality handling requires domain-specific adaptation.
challenge_hooks: How to effectively distinguish semantically similar but logically irrelevant candidates in large-scale video retrieval without expensive retraining?
How to enforce strict persona adherence and prevent hallucinations when generating from multiple heterogeneous video sources?
How to scale cognitive reasoning over massive video collections while maintaining precise temporal grounding without supervised fine-tuning?
How to design retrieval pipelines that bridge the semantic-logical gap between surface-level embeddings and deep reasoning requirements?

items.title: From `May' to `Is': Certainty Distortion in Language Model Rewriting
items.summary: Investigates certainty distortion in LM paraphrasing tasks, where models systematically inflate expressed confidence (e.g., 'may' to 'is') while preserving semantic content. Proposes LLM-as-judge evaluation metric validated against human judgments, finding 75% of outputs distorted with 1.5-2× bias toward overconfidence; effects compound over iterations in medical domains.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly relevant to production LLM evaluation and observability—characterizes a systematic failure mode (certainty inflation) that affects reliability in high-stakes applications like medical/scientific summarization, with practical measurement methodology and mitigation strategies.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly addresses reliability and trustworthiness concerns in LLM outputs relevant to production systems, particularly for document processing pipelines, but lacks clear architectural or engineering solutions.
system.value_rationale: Identifies a critical failure mode in LLM-based extraction and rewriting tasks (certainty distortion) that affects downstream decision-making in high-stakes domains like medical document intelligence. The LLM-as-judge evaluation approach is actionable for building observability into Hermes-type extraction systems, though the paper doesn't provide mitigation strategies or practical deployment guidance.
challenge_hooks: How to detect and measure when language models systematically inflate confidence or certainty in rewritten text while preserving semantic meaning
Building evaluation metrics that capture directional shifts in epistemic markers and hedging language in paraphrasing and simplification tasks
Mitigating systematic certainty distortion in high-stakes domains (medical, scientific, legal) where expressed confidence directly impacts user decision-making
Understanding whether confidence inflation compounds under repeated model transformations and how to prevent cascading certainty drift

items.title: LogNEO: A GPT-Neo Reinforcement Learning Framework for Accurate Real-Time Log Anomaly Detection
items.summary: LogNEO applies GPT-Neo (1.3B, 2048-token context) with position-aware RL fine-tuning via PPO for real-time log anomaly detection. Novel exponentially decaying reward scheme weights early predictions higher and late errors harsher, achieving F1 0.927–0.984 on benchmarks with 45ms latency at 15K events/sec.

system.prefilter_rationale: Production log anomaly detection with concrete deployment architecture (Kafka, Redis, TensorRT), real latency/throughput metrics, and RLHF fine-tuning approach applicable to operational AI systems, though position-aware reward scheme novelty is moderate.
system.enrichment_reason: While the system demonstrates production-relevant latency/throughput metrics and RL fine-tuning for LLM control, log anomaly detection is tangential to core RAG/agentic/document intelligence work and the reward scheme novelty lacks architectural transferability to primary domains.
system.value_rationale: Useful reference for RL-based LLM fine-tuning patterns and real-time inference optimization under tight latency budgets, but the domain (log parsing) doesn't directly apply to retrieval systems, agent orchestration, or structured extraction pipelines.
challenge_hooks: How to design reward functions that reflect variable prediction difficulty across sequence positions in anomaly detection tasks
Extending language model context windows to capture long-range temporal dependencies in system logs without segmentation artifacts
Preventing catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained representations when applying reinforcement learning fine-tuning at scale
Achieving sub-50ms end-to-end latency for real-time anomaly detection at 15K+ events/second in production microservice environments

items.title: Online Agent-as-a-Judge: Situation-Generating Evaluation for Interactive Agents
items.summary: Online Agent-as-a-Judge is a situation-generating evaluation framework for interactive social agents that embeds an in-world evaluator agent to actively elicit criterion-relevant social situations through native dialogue and action interfaces, improving evidence coverage and human agreement compared to passive evaluation methods.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses production evaluation challenge for agentic systems: how to reliably assess LLM agent behavior in interactive multi-turn settings where capability depends on context and prior state—a critical blocker for shipping social/dialogue agents with measurable quality guarantees.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly addresses agent evaluation methodology with a novel evaluation framework relevant to agentic systems, though focused on social agents rather than task-oriented agents typical in production RAG/orchestration pipelines.
system.value_rationale: Provides a practical pattern for evaluating complex agent behaviors through active situation generation rather than static benchmarks, applicable to multi-agent system quality assurance. The in-world evaluator architecture could inform evaluation strategies for production agentic workflows, particularly where agent behavior under varied conditions is critical.
challenge_hooks: How to evaluate interactive social agents when relevant behaviors only manifest under specific social circumstances that passive observation misses
How to systematically generate criterion-relevant test situations for multi-agent social simulations without manual designer effort
How to assess both immediate responses and downstream follow-through behavior in persistent social environments with context-dependent success criteria
How to design evaluation frameworks that survive environment changes while maintaining coverage of designer-specified behavioral properties

items.title: Scaffold Effects on GAIA: A Controlled Comparison
items.summary: Controlled comparison of three agent scaffolds (ReAct, Planner-Actor-Rater, Planner-then-Executor) across five frontier models on GAIA benchmark, quantifying scaffold effects on measured capability with bootstrap confidence intervals and mixed-effects regression. Finds 28-point accuracy gaps within single models, rejecting hypothesis that capable models are less scaffold-sensitive.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses agent evaluation methodology and scaffold design tradeoffs in production agentic systems, with rigorous controlled comparison revealing practical implications for model selection and orchestration architecture choices.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly relevant empirical work on agentic orchestration patterns and their measurable effects on LLM capability, with practical implications for production agent design choices.
system.value_rationale: Provides quantified tradeoffs between three agent scaffolds with statistical rigor, enabling data-driven architectural decisions for agentic workflows. The finding that capability-gap variation within models (28 points) exceeds differences between models challenges assumptions about model selection vs. orchestration optimization in production systems.
challenge_hooks: How much does agent scaffold choice affect measured model capability on general-purpose tasks, and does this effect scale predictably with model tier?
What behavioral patterns distinguish effective scaffolds (tool calls, error recovery, planning-execution separation) and how do they interact with model family vs. capability level?
How should practitioners compare frontier model capabilities across published evaluations when different teams use different agent architectures, and what is the magnitude of the confound?
Which scaffold-model combination minimizes cost-per-correct-answer while maintaining accuracy on multi-step reasoning tasks requiring web search and file reading?

items.title: Calibration of Structured Ignorance Certificates for Diagnosing Unknown Unknowns in Reasoning Models
items.summary: Structured Ignorance Certificates (SICs) are a JSON-formatted output schema trained via GRPO to make LLMs explicitly acknowledge cross-domain knowledge gaps, enumerate required concepts, and propose retrieval queries instead of hallucinating. Achieved 99.46% JSON validity and 0.967 specificity on 7,347 unknown-unknown dataset.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses production concern of hallucination detection and graceful failure modes in LLM systems; the structured output schema and GRPO fine-tuning approach are immediately applicable to RAG and agentic workflows requiring reliable uncertainty quantification.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly addresses structured output reliability and failure mode detection in production LLMs, with explicit relevance to RAG triggering and hallucination prevention—core production concerns.
system.value_rationale: Provides a concrete schema-based approach to detect when LLMs lack knowledge and should defer to retrieval, reducing hallucination risks in agentic systems. The GRPO fine-tuning methodology and JSON validity metrics offer immediately applicable techniques for improving structured output reliability in production RAG pipelines.
challenge_hooks: How can LLMs recognize and explicitly output when questions exceed their representational coverage across multiple domains?
How to train models to produce structured, actionable epistemic metadata rather than confident hallucinations on out-of-distribution cross-domain queries?
What reward design and fine-tuning approach enables reliable JSON-formatted uncertainty communication with measurable concept specificity and retrieval utility?
How to evaluate whether a model's generated uncertainty outputs genuinely reflect internal paraphrase-based divergence in reasoning?

items.title: Intrinsic Selection and Particle Resampling for Inference-Time Scaling Beyond Domain Verifiability
items.summary: Framework for inference-time scaling using intrinsic statistics (tail entropy, length distributions) of parallel samples to enable solution selection and step-level resampling without external verifiers, reward models, or ground-truth access across math, coding, CAD, and clinical domains.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly relevant to inference-time compute allocation and solution quality ranking without external verification—applicable to agentic workflows, document intelligence tasks, and production systems where ground-truth verification is unavailable or expensive.
system.enrichment_reason: Inference-time scaling without external verifiers addresses a real production concern for agentic systems, but the framing as 'intrinsic selection' is orthogonal to core RAG/retrieval/orchestration work and lacks demonstrated cost-latency tradeoffs versus standard verifier approaches.
system.value_rationale: Directly applicable to agent evaluation and multi-step reasoning in production systems where ground truth is unavailable; however, the value is primarily in the inference scaling strategy rather than the core RAG/agent architecture patterns you build, making this a secondary optimization concern rather than foundational.
concepts: Tail entropy and length-adjusted confidence metrics
challenge_hooks: How to scale inference-time computation in open-ended domains without access to expensive external verifiers or trained reward models
Identifying high-quality solutions from parallel samples using only intrinsic model statistics (entropy, length) without ground-truth verification
Performing step-level resampling and guiding generation toward correct reasoning trajectories in hard-to-verify tasks with systematic reasoning failures
Correcting faulty initial assumptions and enforcing multidimensional constraints in complex reasoning tasks using privileged guidance without explicit verification

items.title: sGPO: Trading Inference FLOPs for Training Efficiency in RLVR
items.summary: sGPO trades cheap inference FLOPs for training efficiency in RLVR by using offline profiling to determine per-query rollout group sizes, data filtering, and curriculum ordering, reducing total compute by 2.5-3.1× while maintaining accuracy on reasoning tasks.

system.prefilter_rationale: Direct applicability to production RL training pipelines; addresses real compute efficiency problem in RLVR systems with actionable heuristic (inverse success rate for group sizing) and demonstrates 3x training efficiency gains—immediately relevant for scaling agentic systems and verifiable reasoning workflows.
system.enrichment_reason: Relevant to production LLM optimization but focused on training-time efficiency rather than inference serving or retrieval patterns central to RAG/agentic work.
system.value_rationale: Provides actionable insights on compute-efficiency tradeoffs for reasoning tasks during training, useful for planning fine-tuning pipelines; however, the offline profiling approach and curriculum design are less immediately applicable than inference optimization or retrieval system improvements for current production workflows.
concepts: Offline profiling and empirical success rate estimation
Adaptive group size allocation via inverse success rate
Sample efficiency and advantage signal optimization
challenge_hooks: How to allocate computational budgets efficiently in RLVR when fixed rollout counts waste training on trivial and unsolvable queries
Designing curriculum and data selection strategies that exploit the asymmetry between cheap inference and expensive training compute
Determining optimal per-query group sizes in policy optimization without blind first epochs or online recomputation
Maximizing sample efficiency by extracting maximum advantage signal per generated rollout in reasoning model training

items.title: TRIAGE: Dialectical Reasoning for Explainable Risk Prediction on Irregularly Sampled Medical Time Series with LLMs
items.summary: TRIAGE addresses risk polarization in LLM-based clinical risk prediction on irregularly sampled medical time series by using dialectical reasoning over competing outcomes. It generates outcome-specific rationales and derives calibrated continuous risk scores from implicit probabilities, achieving 3.3% AUPRC improvement and 81% calibration error reduction.

system.prefilter_rationale: Production-relevant: addresses calibration and interpretability in LLM-based clinical systems, demonstrates concrete engineering pattern (dialectical reasoning for risk grounding) applicable to document intelligence + agentic workflows in healthcare domains.
system.enrichment_reason: While the paper demonstrates LLM application to a structured prediction task with observable improvements in calibration and explainability, the domain is specialized clinical time series prediction rather than core NLP/RAG/agentic work, and the technical contribution centers on prompt engineering for reasoning rather than production system architecture.
system.value_rationale: The dialectical reasoning pattern for generating competing outcome rationales could inform multi-perspective prompting in agentic systems, and the calibration recovery technique is relevant for LLM-as-judge applications. However, the irregular time series handling and clinical focus limit transferability to document intelligence and retrieval pipelines.
challenge_hooks: How to extract well-calibrated continuous risk scores from LLM predictions for clinical decision support
Preventing risk polarization when LLMs generate reasoning before predictions
Generating balanced, evidence-grounded clinical explanations that weigh alternative outcomes
Handling irregular temporal medical data with sparse measurements while producing interpretable outputs

items.title: Decoy-Calibrated Failure Audits for Language Models
items.summary: Janus is a procedure for auditing LLM failure modes that separates explanation discovery from reporting. It uses decoy descriptors (fake properties with same prevalence but random assignment) to calibrate error-lift thresholds and requires replication on holdout data before confirming audit findings.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly applicable to production LLM evaluation workflows; addresses critical problem of distinguishing spurious correlations from genuine failure modes when auditing model behavior—essential for reliable system monitoring and incident diagnosis.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly applicable to production LLM evaluation and observability, addressing rigorous failure mode detection critical for production systems, though tilted toward evaluation methodology over immediate deployment concerns.
system.value_rationale: Provides a concrete framework for avoiding spurious failure discovery in LLM audits—a key risk when evaluating RAG/agentic systems in production. The decoy-calibration approach prevents overconfident claims about model failures, essential for making reliable deployment and monitoring decisions.
challenge_hooks: How to distinguish genuine LLM failure modes from spurious patterns discovered through multiple testing of candidate explanations
Preventing false positives in model audits when many candidate error descriptors are evaluated against limited evaluation data
Validating that discovered error slices generalize beyond the discovery split before reporting them as audit findings

items.title: INFUSER: Influence-Guided Self-Evolution Improves Reasoning
items.summary: INFUSER is an iterative co-training framework for self-evolution where a Generator creates questions from unstructured documents and a Solver improves by training on them. An optimizer-aware influence score rewards the Generator for proposing questions that actually improve the Solver on target distributions, using DuGRPO for stable training.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly relevant self-improvement framework for LLMs with practical engineering contributions (influence-aware curriculum generation, DuGRPO variant) applicable to production reasoning systems; strong empirical results on math/coding with clear architectural patterns for agentic data generation.
system.enrichment_reason: Self-evolution frameworks and influence-guided training are relevant to agentic system design and LLM improvement, but the paper's focus on synthetic question generation from documents is a narrow application with limited direct production applicability.
system.value_rationale: The influence-scoring mechanism for evaluating which training examples actually improve model performance on target distributions could inform evaluation strategies for RAG-generated synthetic data or agent feedback loops. However, the co-training pattern is more academic-exploration oriented than directly applicable to production document intelligence or retrieval systems.
challenge_hooks: How to scale reasoning improvement without expensive teacher annotations or curated datasets
Designing reward signals that measure whether generated training examples actually improve model performance on target tasks
Training data generators to propose curriculum-appropriate questions rather than merely hard ones
Stabilizing GRPO training with noisy, continuous influence scores in co-evolving systems

items.title: A Unifying Lens on Reward Uncertainty in RLHF
items.summary: Unifying framework for reward uncertainty in RLHF via distributional reward models. Shows that both Bayesian marginalization and KL-DRO yield closed-form effective rewards using moment generating functions, unifying prior ensemble aggregation heuristics (mean, WCO, UWO) as limits/truncations of a single expression to mitigate reward hacking.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses reward hacking in RLHF—a critical production failure mode—with a unified mathematical framework that explains existing heuristics (ensemble aggregation, WCO, UWO) and provides principled guidance for uncertainty-aware reward modeling in deployed systems.
system.enrichment_reason: Addresses reward model uncertainty in RLHF, which is relevant to agentic system safety and evaluation, but focuses on theoretical unification of existing methods rather than new architectural patterns or production deployment strategies.
system.value_rationale: Provides useful formalization for understanding reward aggregation heuristics (mean/WCO/UWO) in production RLHF pipelines and reward hacking mitigation, applicable when building reliable agent reward signals. However, limited actionability without concrete implementation guidance for integrating distributional rewards into serving or inference.
challenge_hooks: How to principally incorporate reward model uncertainty into RLHF optimization without ad-hoc ensemble aggregation rules
Mitigating reward hacking by designing pessimistic objectives that downweight uncertain reward regions
Unifying disparate ensemble-based and Bayesian approaches to distributional reward modeling under a single mathematical framework

items.title: Late-Layer Fusion is Enough: Dual-Path Vision Token Routing for Multimodal Large Language Models under Visual Saturation
items.summary: Proposes DPVR-LF, a modality-asymmetric architecture for MLLMs that routes vision tokens through a shallow side branch after saturation (~layer 18) while text tokens traverse deep layers, fusing only at final layer. Achieves 28% latency reduction with 3% trainable parameters while maintaining competitive performance on standard benchmarks.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly applicable to production MLLM deployment: proposes concrete architectural optimization (late-layer fusion) that reduces compute overhead by ~3% parameters while maintaining performance—actionable for latency/cost tradeoffs in document intelligence and multimodal RAG systems.
system.enrichment_reason: While the latency optimization is production-relevant, the work is primarily a vision-language architecture paper focused on model training efficiency rather than retrieval, agentic systems, or document intelligence—the core domains of applied LLM deployment.
system.value_rationale: The dual-path routing and visual saturation concepts could inform multimodal RAG systems handling document images, but the paper's focus on MLLM architecture training rather than inference serving, retrieval patterns, or production deployment makes it peripheral to immediate practical concerns in agent building or document intelligence pipelines.
challenge_hooks: How to reduce inference latency in MLLMs without sacrificing multimodal understanding quality
Why do vision and text tokens require different computational depths in decoder-only MLLMs
How to implement efficient modality-conditional routing with minimal architectural changes to existing MLLM pipelines
Can a single fusion layer suffice for maintaining strong vision-language alignment in deep transformers

items.title: Reasoning Arena: Trace Tournaments When Verifiable Rewards Fall Short
items.summary: Reasoning Arena addresses inefficiency in RLVR by detecting non-diverse reward groups (all-correct/all-incorrect) that yield zero gradients, routing them to LLM-judge trace tournaments instead. Uses live opponent selection and Bradley-Terry modeling to efficiently extract fine-grained reasoning preferences, achieving 7.6% performance gains and 27-41% training acceleration.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses a core production problem in LLM reasoning training (uninformative reward signals in RL pipelines), proposes a practical architectural solution (trace tournaments with Bradley-Terry ranking) that avoids quadratic complexity, and demonstrates significant compute efficiency gains (27-41% acceleration, 50% generation savings) relevant to scaling agentic reasoning systems.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly relevant to LLM evaluation and preference learning for reasoning tasks, with production-applicable techniques for handling sparse reward signals in agentic reasoning systems.
system.value_rationale: The trace tournament approach and Bradley-Terry modeling for extracting fine-grained reasoning preferences is actionable for improving agent training efficiency in production RAG/agentic systems where verifiable rewards are sparse. The 27-41% training acceleration and live opponent selection pattern are directly applicable to building better reasoning-capable agents.
challenge_hooks: How to extract learning signals from reasoning traces that receive identical verifiable rewards despite differing in quality
Reducing wasted compute from non-diverse reward groups in RLVR training pipelines
Scaling pairwise trace comparisons for judge-based rewards without quadratic inference cost
Adaptive routing between outcome-based verifiers and intermediate reasoning judgments for efficient policy optimization

items.title: Correct Looks Better: Pairwise Comparisons Reveal Accuracy Rankings
items.summary: Study demonstrating that pairwise comparison rankings of generative models achieve >0.9 Spearman correlation with ground-truth accuracy rankings across five benchmarks. Bradley-Terry aggregation outperforms direct evaluation with weak judges; style/bias have minor effects despite 60% non-discriminative pairs.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses LLM evaluation methodology with production implications: validates pairwise comparison + Elo aggregation for model ranking, identifies specific judge bias failure modes (echo effect), and provides empirical evidence for evaluation framework selection in production ML systems.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly applicable to LLM evaluation methodology for production systems, but focuses on ranking models rather than evaluating individual outputs or agentic behavior.
system.value_rationale: Pairwise comparison aggregation is immediately useful for model selection in production (choosing between Claude, GPT-4, Llama variants for RAG/agent backends) and provides a robust framework for LLM-as-judge evaluation when direct scoring is noisy. However, the work's emphasis on ranking models at scale (not ranking individual generation quality) limits depth of applicability for document intelligence or agent evaluation tasks.
challenge_hooks: How to rank LLMs when ground truth is unavailable or expensive to obtain
Validating whether pairwise preference rankings reflect actual model quality vs superficial stylistic cues
Improving model evaluation when judge models are weaker than candidate models being evaluated
Understanding and mitigating bias in LLM-based pairwise comparison evaluation systems

items.title: Memory Beyond Recall: A Dual-Process Cognitive Memory System for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.summary: DCPM: A dual-process cognitive memory architecture for LLM agents that organizes memory hierarchically from raw inputs through atomic facts, belief trajectories, and identity to cross-domain schemas and intentions. System 1 synchronously records belief revisions as doubly-linked supersedes chains; System 2 asynchronously induces schemas and detects cross-domain behavioral patterns.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses production memory architectures for agentic systems with concrete hierarchical design (belief trajectories, schema induction, cross-domain abstraction) and dual-process computational patterns that map to engineering tradeoffs between latency (System 1) and reasoning depth (System 2)—immediately applicable to RAG-augmented agent design.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly addresses agent memory architectures and state management for multi-turn agentic systems, with practical implications for LangGraph-based workflows and agent evaluation, though the dual-process framing is more cognitive science than engineering-focused.
system.value_rationale: The hierarchical memory organization (raw inputs → atomic facts → belief trajectories → schemas) and asynchronous pattern detection offer concrete design patterns for stateful agent systems; the doubly-linked supersedes chains for belief revision provide a testable approach to tracking agent reasoning evolution across interactions, valuable for observability and multi-turn agent reliability.
challenge_hooks: How to track and retrieve user belief evolution over long sessions when embedding similarity collapses intermediate states and causal links
Detecting latent cross-domain behavioral patterns that are behaviorally similar but semantically distant across unrelated life domains
Separating fast online memory encoding from slow offline abstraction in agent systems to enable implicit personalization reasoning

items.title: TABVERSE: Benchmarking Cross-Format Table Understanding in LLMs and VLMs
items.summary: TabVerse is a controlled multimodal benchmark for evaluating table understanding in LLMs and VLMs across aligned HTML, Markdown, LaTeX formats and rendered images. It isolates representation effects on three tasks: QA, structural understanding, and reconstruction, with 700 balanced samples tagged by difficulty and category.

system.prefilter_rationale: TABVERSE directly addresses a production concern in document intelligence pipelines: how table representation format (HTML, Markdown, LaTeX, images) affects LLM/VLM performance on extraction and reasoning tasks, enabling practitioners to make informed choices about preprocessing and format conversion in extraction systems.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly relevant to document intelligence and extraction workflows, particularly for evaluating how LLMs handle structured tabular data across formats—a critical component of production document processing pipelines.
system.value_rationale: Provides empirical benchmarking data on format robustness and representation effects for table understanding, which informs architectural decisions on how to represent tables in RAG systems and document extraction pipelines. Useful for evaluating whether to normalize table formats or use multimodal approaches in production systems.
challenge_hooks: How do different table formats (HTML, Markdown, LaTeX) and modalities (text vs. rendered images) affect model performance when table content is held constant?
Can LLMs and VLMs reliably extract structural information from tables and reconstruct them in syntactically valid formats?
What representation-specific failure modes emerge in table reasoning, and how do they vary across question types and difficulty levels?

items.title: End-to-End Context Compression at Scale
items.summary: Latent Context Language Models (LCLMs) enable end-to-end encoder-decoder context compression at scale, achieving new Pareto frontiers for memory/latency/accuracy tradeoffs. Models trained on 350B tokens with systematic architecture search and multi-stage training recipe support efficient long-context inference and agentic reasoning.

system.prefilter_rationale: Direct production relevance to long-context inference bottlenecks; encoder-decoder compression architecture with measurable accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs and agent integration patterns are immediately applicable to RAG and agentic systems at scale.
system.enrichment_reason: Context compression directly addresses production RAG latency and cost constraints, while the agentic reasoning application aligns with core workflow optimization.
system.value_rationale: Encoder-decoder compression patterns could improve retrieval-augmented context efficiency and reduce inference costs for long-context agentic systems. The Pareto frontier framing (memory/latency/accuracy) is immediately actionable for deployment tradeoff decisions, though the focus on model architecture search is less directly applicable than empirical compression techniques.
challenge_hooks: How to reduce KV cache memory overhead in long-context LLM inference without substantial quality degradation
Designing general-purpose, task-agnostic context compressors that preserve base model capabilities across heterogeneous inputs
Balancing compression speed, memory usage, and downstream task accuracy on the Pareto frontier for production systems
Enabling efficient agentic reasoning over long contexts through adaptive selective decompression of compressed segments

items.title: Correlation Is Not Enough: Embedding Human Metadata for Individual Causal Discovery
items.summary: Addresses embedding geometry errors in biomedical language models causing false causal inference in behavioral models. Proposes contrastive learning with knowledge-graph-mined hard negatives to improve cross-domain discrimination from 0% to 39.2%, achieving 133x latency reduction via optimized inference.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses embedding quality in retrieval systems with production-grade solutions (contrastive fine-tuning, hard negative mining, latency optimization), critical for RAG correctness and relevant to document intelligence systems where false causal associations corrupt downstream reasoning.
system.enrichment_reason: While the paper addresses embedding quality and inference optimization (relevant), the focus on biomedical causal discovery and behavioral models is orthogonal to RAG, agentic systems, and document intelligence workflows.
system.value_rationale: The contrastive learning approach and knowledge-graph integration for hard negatives could inform embedding model selection criteria, but the biomedical domain specificity and causal inference framing limit direct applicability to production NLP/RAG systems.
concepts: hard negative mining from knowledge graphs
foundation models for individual behavior modeling
challenge_hooks: How to prevent false causal edges in behavioral models due to embedding proximity errors across biomedical and non-biomedical domains
Embedding quality metrics and contrastive training strategies for domain-aware semantic similarity that distinguishes correlation from causation
Production deployment of biomedical embeddings: latency optimization and hardware-specific inference tuning for real-time graph reasoning

items.title: Learning to Attack and Defend: Adaptive Red Teaming of Language Models via GRPO
items.summary: AdvGRPO is a co-training framework using GRPO with dense multi-channel rewards and decoupled advantage normalization for simultaneous attacker-defender optimization in LLM red teaming. Introduces closed-loop multi-turn attacks with per-turn rewards and curriculum-based training to produce transferable jailbreaks while improving defender robustness.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly applicable to production LLM safety: demonstrates practical RL-based red teaming methodology with concrete training curriculum, handles real deployment concern of adaptive adversaries, and provides transferable attack patterns useful for stress-testing production systems.
system.enrichment_reason: While the adversarial robustness framing has tangential relevance to production LLM safety, this paper focuses on attack/defense research mechanics rather than practical production observability, evaluation, or defense patterns applicable to deployed systems.
system.value_rationale: Limited direct application to production RAG/agent systems. Most relevant only if building safety evaluation frameworks or adversarial testing pipelines, but the GRPO mechanics are specialized research rather than actionable engineering patterns for practitioners shipping document intelligence or agentic workflows.
challenge_hooks: How can reinforcement learning be stabilized for joint attacker-defender optimization when prior GRPO applications in this domain reported instability?
How do you design reward signals and training curricula that enable attackers to discover novel jailbreaks while defenders generalize beyond static adversarial datasets?
What closed-loop multi-turn attack strategies can language models learn when conditioned on defender responses, versus open-loop attack generation?
How can red-teaming frameworks produce transferable adversarial prompts that successfully attack unseen defender models and out-of-distribution objectives?

items.title: Multi-Turn Evaluation of Deep Research Agents Under Process-Level Feedback
items.summary: Multi-turn evaluation framework for deep research agents using process-level feedback. Introduces Research Gap Inference (RGI) to analyze rubric patterns and identify research-strategy gaps. Finds agents improve 88-151 points with single feedback round but regress on 24% of criteria in subsequent turns, showing multi-turn improvement remains challenging.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses agent evaluation and multi-turn refinement patterns—core to production agentic systems—with actionable findings on feedback mechanisms, failure modes in iterative improvement, and architectural limitations relevant to building reliable research agents.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly addresses agentic system evaluation and multi-turn reasoning patterns with practical findings on feedback mechanisms and performance degradation, highly relevant to production agent orchestration; limited immediate applicability since research agents differ from retrieval/RAG agents in scope.
system.value_rationale: The multi-turn degradation finding (regression on 24% of criteria) and process-level feedback analysis provide actionable insights for designing robust agent workflows and evaluation harnesses. The Research Gap Inference pattern is architecturally relevant for understanding where agentic systems fail under iterative refinement, informing observability and feedback loop design in production systems.
challenge_hooks: How do agentic research systems improve when given iterative feedback, and why do gains not compound across multiple turns?
How to diagnose and address gaps in agent research strategy (source selection, scope framing, subtopic coverage) beyond surface-level content failures?
Why do agents regress on previously satisfied criteria when revising full reports to address remaining gaps, and how can this be mitigated?

items.title: Data Synthesis and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Low-Resource NMT: A Case Study on Q'eqchi' Mayan
items.summary: Proposes distribution-aware synthetic data generation and LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning for bootstrapping neural machine translation of Q'eqchi' Mayan without web-scraping. Demonstrates synthetic data teaches morphology and word order effectively but reveals structural-semantic gap; MTL causes negative transfer under purely synthetic constraints.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly applicable case study on PEFT (LoRA) for low-resource NLP, synthetic data generation tradeoffs, and multi-task learning failure modes—practical insights on parameter efficiency, data quality gaps, and curriculum learning that inform production RAG/extraction systems for under-resourced domains.
system.enrichment_reason: While parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) is production-relevant, this work focuses on low-resource NMT for an indigenous language without direct applicability to core domains (RAG, document intelligence, agentic systems) and the synthetic data approach is task-specific rather than transferable.
system.value_rationale: LoRA techniques could inform parameter-efficient adaptation in production RAG/agent systems, and the structural-semantic gap insight has minor relevance for understanding fine-tuning failure modes. However, the paper's primary contribution (synthetic data for low-resource NMT) sits outside active work areas and lacks production-serving, inference, or orchestration considerations.
concepts: Synthetic data generation via rule-based templates
Focal loss optimization for morphologically rich languages
Multi-task learning with auxiliary POS/semantic tagging
challenge_hooks: How to bootstrap NMT for digitally low-resource languages without violating data sovereignty via web-scraping
Teaching complex agglutinative morphology and non-SVO word order with synthetic training data alone
Resolving the structural-semantic gap where models learn grammar but lack lexical grounding in synthetic-only training

items.title: Trainable Smooth-Rotation Transforms with Learned Channel Scales for LLM Quantization
items.summary: Post-training quantization method for LLMs using trainable smooth-rotation transforms with quantile-robust scaling policies and learned channel scales. Addresses activation outlier problem in W4A4 quantization through parameterized equivalent transformations, achieving 18.5% error reduction on LLaMA-3.2-1B via constrained gradient-based optimization.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses production LLM quantization challenges (W4A4, activation outliers) with practical post-training optimization techniques applicable to inference cost reduction, a core concern for shipping LLM systems.
system.enrichment_reason: While LLM quantization is relevant to production deployment, this paper focuses on post-training optimization techniques for weight-activation quantization without addressing practical inference serving concerns like latency, throughput, memory overhead, or real-world deployment tradeoffs.
system.value_rationale: Applicable if you're optimizing quantized model accuracy before serving, but the paper's focus on mathematical transforms and activation outlier handling doesn't directly advance RAG, agentic systems, document intelligence, or the engineering patterns needed for production LLM systems. More relevant to model optimization than system building.

Balancing channel-wise scaling strength (α) and robust activation statistics (quantiles) in equivalent-transform quantization methods
Learning optimal scaling parameters via gradient descent when quantization operations are non-differentiable
Systematically selecting and generalizing layer-wise quantization policies across full LLM decoder networks

items.title: RKSC: Reasoning-Aware KV Cache Sharing and Confident Early Exit for Multi-Step LLM Inference
items.summary: RKSC is a training-free inference framework for multi-branch LLM reasoning that eliminates redundancies through attention-similarity KV cache sharing (ASKS), confidence-gated early exit (CGEE), and reasoning-selective block cache management. Achieves 3.008× mean speedup with 0.37% error rate across five model families.

system.enrichment_reason: Direct applicability to production LLM serving optimization with measurable latency/throughput gains, though KV cache tuning is a narrow efficiency concern versus broader agentic workflow architecture.
system.value_rationale: RKSC's training-free optimization approach (ASKS + CGEE) is immediately applicable to multi-step reasoning pipelines common in agentic systems, reducing inference costs without model retraining. The 3× speedup justifies evaluation for latency-critical retrieval-augmented reasoning tasks, though value depends on whether your bottleneck is compute cost versus orchestration overhead.

Per-layer entropy stabilization for early termination
Block-level cache eviction with attention-weighted priority
Batched decode with prefix reuse generalization

How to exploit semantic similarity beyond token-exact prefix matching for cache reuse
How to detect and skip unnecessary verification passes when model confidence is already decisive
How to manage unbounded KV cache growth in deep tree search reasoning without accuracy loss

items.title: Bittensor Agent Arenas as a Trajectory Primitive: Distilling a Shopping Agent from ShoppingBench Subnet Traces
items.summary: Bittensor subnet mechanism (SN15/ShoppingBench) for manufacturing judged agentic trajectories via incentive-aligned competition. Distills Qwen3-4B shopping agent from filtered subnet traces using multi-stage SFT+RL pipeline, achieving 42.7% ASR on held-out eval versus 18.0% base and 48.7% synthetic baseline.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses trajectory quality as a production bottleneck for agentic post-training, demonstrates a practical incentive-aligned corpus-generation mechanism with concrete architectural choices (race mechanism, judge design, leak-cluster filtering), and provides actionable empirical results on small-model distillation with reproducible baselines—core to shipping agentic systems at scale.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly addresses agentic systems and agent evaluation through a novel data generation mechanism (incentive-aligned trajectory collection), though the Bittensor-specific infrastructure and shopping domain limit broader applicability.
system.value_rationale: Provides a production-grade pattern for bootstrapping agent training data via competitive filtering rather than synthetic generation, with concrete SFT+RL pipeline results. The trajectory distillation approach is transferable to other agentic domains, though the Bittensor mechanism itself is domain-specific infrastructure.
challenge_hooks: How to source high-quality judged multi-turn trajectories for agentic post-training without synthetic data collapse or unfiltered production noise
Designing economic mechanisms that incentivize diverse agent policy discovery while producing anti-memorized held-out evaluation
Filtering raw agent arena trajectories to separate truly agentic behavior from shortcut/sub-task patterns before SFT training
Scaling small open models (4B parameters) to competitive performance on tool-use benchmarks through trajectory quality and RL recipe optimization

items.title: Unsupervised Style Representation Learning for AI-Text Detection via Paraphrase Inversion
items.summary: Proposes LUSR, an unsupervised method for learning style representations via paraphrase inversion to detect AI-generated text. Freezes semantic encoder during training to force style encoder to capture non-semantic features. Evaluates via few-shot prototype matching and zero-shot DeepSVDD-based detection, achieving competitive performance with robustness to paraphrasing attacks.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly relevant to production AI-text detection systems; unsupervised style representation learning addresses practical deployment constraints (label scarcity, zero-shot generalization) and adversarial robustness concerns that impact real-world detector reliability.
system.enrichment_reason: While the paper addresses AI-text detection (a relevant problem), the technical approach focuses on unsupervised representation learning and anomaly detection rather than production-applicable document intelligence or retrieval systems.
system.value_rationale: Marginally useful for understanding style-based detection robustness, but the paraphrase-inversion methodology and zero-shot anomaly detection (DeepSVDD) are not core to building RAG systems, agentic workflows, or document intelligence pipelines that drive current work.
challenge_hooks: How to learn writing style representations without authorship labels for detecting AI-generated text
Detecting machine-generated text that resists paraphrasing attacks and generalizes across unseen LLMs
Separating stylistic features from semantic content in text representations
Enabling zero-shot detection of AI text when no in-distribution reference samples are available

items.title: $τ$-Rec: A Verifiable Benchmark for Agentic Recommender Systems
items.summary: τ-Rec introduces a verifiable benchmark for agentic recommender systems using deterministic catalog predicates, reveal-tagged elicitation (RTE), and pass^k reliability metrics to replace subjective LLM-as-judge evaluation. Evaluation of six LLM models exposes a reliability cliff, with best performance at ~57% pass^1 and ~35% pass^4.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses production evaluation of agentic systems with verifiable metrics and concrete reliability benchmarks—core to shipping reliable conversational agents in practice.
system.enrichment_reason: Directly addresses agentic system evaluation and reliability measurement, core concerns for production agentic workflows, though the recommender-system-specific domain is tangential to primary focus areas.
system.value_rationale: Provides a concrete reproducible evaluation framework (deterministic predicates, RTE, pass^k metrics) that could be adapted for evaluating other agentic systems beyond recommendations. The reliability cliff finding is actionable for understanding LLM model selection tradeoffs in production agent deployments.
concepts: verifiable rewards with typed catalog predicates
challenge_hooks: How to evaluate agentic recommender systems without expensive, non-deterministic LLM-as-judge scoring?
How to force conversational agents to elicit user preferences through dialogue rather than pattern-matching against disclosed constraints?
How to measure reliability and consistency of LLM agents across repeated trials, not just capability on single attempts?
How to incorporate responsible-AI policies (age-gating, transparency, disclosure) as first-class evaluation objectives in recommendation systems?

items.title: Supervised Fine-tuning with Synthetic Rationale Data Hurts Real-World Disease Prediction
items.summary: Supervised fine-tuning with synthetic rationales degrades disease prediction performance compared to label-only training across 504 configurations on ADRD prediction. Despite high-quality, medically accurate rationales, the structural conflict between narrative plausibility and discriminative optimization causes this failure.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly relevant to production document intelligence and clinical NLP systems—demonstrates a critical failure mode in synthetic rationale supervision that affects real-world deployment decisions, with actionable guidance on when rationale-based training helps vs. hurts performance.

How to distinguish between high-quality explanations and effective training signals for medical AI
Reconciling narrative coherence requirements with discriminative learning objectives in healthcare prediction tasks
Trade-offs between model transparency through rationales and raw prediction accuracy in high-stakes domains

items.title: Agentic Hybrid RAG for Evidence-Grounded Muon Collider Analysis
items.summary: Agentic hybrid RAG system for muon collider scientific QA combining BM25 sparse retrieval, dense embeddings, and agentic query decomposition. Constructs first muon collider benchmark with evidence-grounded evaluation metrics for retrieval and answer generation in HEP.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses agentic RAG patterns (hybrid retrieval, query decomposition, evidence expansion) with production evaluation against baselines and systematic benchmarking; domain-specific application demonstrates architectural decisions transferable to other evidence-grounded QA systems.
system.enrichment_reason: Demonstrates advanced agentic RAG patterns (query decomposition, hybrid retrieval) with production-relevant evaluation methodology, but domain-specific physics application limits generalizability to core work.

concepts: graded evaluation metrics (gNDCG, hallucination rate, key-point coverage)
challenge_hooks: How to integrate sparse keyword matching with dense semantic retrieval for terminology-heavy scientific domains without retrieval drift
Evaluating faithfulness and evidence grounding in LLM-generated scientific answers across multi-document synthesis tasks
Decomposing complex scientific queries spanning multiple subfields (accelerator physics, detector instrumentation, phenomenology) into retrievable evidence chunks
Building domain-specific RAG benchmarks with fine-grained relevance labels and answer-level metrics beyond standard ROUGE/RAGAS

items.title: ERAlign: Energy-based Representation Alignment of GNNs and LLMs on Text-attributed Graphs
items.summary: ERAlign proposes energy-based representation alignment for GNNs and LLMs on text-attributed graphs. Uses Cramér distance and Energy Discrepancy minimization to enforce distributional consistency across layer-wise alignment, achieving SOTA on 8 benchmarks with improved label efficiency and cross-task transferability.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly applicable to production RAG and document intelligence systems that combine graph structures with LLM embeddings for retrieval and entity linking; the distributional alignment framework addresses real engineering challenges in multi-modal representation fusion for knowledge-grounded applications.
system.enrichment_reason: While the paper addresses GNN-LLM integration on text-attributed graphs, the energy-based alignment approach is theoretically focused without clear production relevance to RAG, agentic systems, or document intelligence workflows.
system.value_rationale: The work is tangentially relevant only if you're building hybrid retrieval systems that combine graph-structured knowledge with LLM representations; however, the energy-based distribution matching technique lacks demonstrated applicability to practical production concerns like latency, cost, or failure mode handling that define the profile's engineering focus.
challenge_hooks: How to align representations from heterogeneous modalities (graphs and text) in a principled probabilistic framework
Reducing sampling costs in EBM training while maintaining theoretical guarantees for distribution matching
Achieving layer-wise alignment between shallow GNNs and deep LLMs with consistent distributional properties
Enabling zero-shot cross-task transfer and label efficiency when combining structural and textual signals

items.title: Advancing the State-of-the-Art in Empirical Privacy Auditing
items.summary: Novel empirical privacy auditing framework for LLMs using synthetic canaries via high-temperature sampling and auxiliary model-based data auditing to detect memorization in fine-tuned models and synthetic data generation, with systematic study of model capacity and canary entropy effects.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly applicable to production RAG/document systems: empirical privacy auditing methodology for LLM fine-tuning is critical for shipping systems on sensitive data, with actionable techniques (synthetic canaries, auxiliary model auditing) and measurable privacy risk quantification.
system.enrichment_reason: Privacy auditing is peripherally relevant to production LLM systems, but this paper's focus on memorization detection and synthetic canaries addresses a research concern rather than a shipping practitioner's immediate priority.

challenge_hooks: How to design effective canary examples for privacy auditing that balance identifiability with naturalness without accessing sensitive training data
Detecting subtle, diffuse privacy leakage in synthetic data that spreads across token distributions rather than appearing as verbatim memorization
Measuring memorization risk when fine-tuning LLMs on sensitive domain-specific data with limited parameter-efficient methods like LoRA
Understanding how model capacity (LoRA rank) and data entropy interact to influence privacy leakage and memorization in parameter-efficient training

items.title: Benchmarking Knowledge Editing using Logical Rules
items.summary: Novel benchmark for evaluating knowledge editing in LLMs using automatically mined logical rules from knowledge graphs. Addresses gap where existing KE methods handle direct edits well but fail on logically entailed consequences, showing up to 24% performance drop on multi-hop reasoning.

system.prefilter_rationale: Production LLMs require knowledge editing for factual currency; this benchmark directly addresses a critical gap in evaluating whether edits propagate logically, exposing real failure modes (ROME/FT missing entailment) that impact deployed systems relying on consistent knowledge graphs.
system.enrichment_reason: Knowledge editing benchmarking is tangentially related to RAG and document intelligence but represents a niche evaluation problem with limited production applicability compared to core priorities like retrieval optimization, agent reasoning, or extraction reliability.
system.value_rationale: Useful for understanding LLM brittleness under logical consistency constraints, which could inform agent verification pipelines or fact-grounded extraction systems. However, knowledge editing itself is rarely deployed in production RAG systems—most handle evolving facts through retrieval updates rather than in-model edits, limiting immediate actionability.
challenge_hooks: How can we evaluate whether knowledge edits in LLMs propagate correctly through logically entailed facts and multi-hop reasoning chains?
Why do current knowledge editing methods succeed at direct fact insertion but fail to maintain consistency across related interconnected knowledge?
How to automatically generate scalable, domain-agnostic test cases for knowledge editing evaluation without manual curation?
What evaluation framework can expose weaknesses in KE approaches for real-world scenarios where assertions have interdependencies?

items.title: Detecting Knowledge Gaps from Conversational AI Interactions Using Curriculum Prerequisite Graphs
items.summary: Pipeline mapping student questions from conversational AI teaching assistants to curriculum topics using few-shot text classification grounded in GPT-4-extracted prerequisite knowledge graphs. Achieves 80% accuracy on 1,340 questions from 164 students; topic-level question volume correlates significantly with self-reported difficulty (ρ=0.491, p=0.008), demonstrating actionable signals for knowledge gap detection.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly relevant as a production pattern for LLM-based educational systems: demonstrates practical pipeline (few-shot classification + knowledge graph grounding) for extracting actionable signals from conversational AI logs, with validated correlation to student learning outcomes—applicable to building observability into agent systems.
system.enrichment_reason: While the paper demonstrates conversational AI interaction analysis and LLM-based classification, it targets educational assessment rather than production NLP systems, retrieval architectures, or agentic workflows central to your applied work.
system.value_rationale: The few-shot classification pipeline using GPT-4 and the prerequisite graph extraction methodology could inform conversational analysis in broader RAG systems, but the educational domain specificity and lack of deployment-scale considerations (latency, cost, serving architecture) limits direct applicability to your production AI systems.
challenge_hooks: How to extract actionable diagnostic signals from free-form conversational student questions without structured item responses?
How to map unstructured course interactions to curriculum structure to identify topic-level knowledge gaps at scale?
How to validate that classifier-mapped question streams reflect genuine student difficulty independent of the classifier itself?

items.title: K-Forcing: Joint Next-K-Token Decoding via Push-Forward Language Modeling
items.summary: K-Forcing proposes push-forward language modeling for joint next-k-token decoding via progressive self-forcing distillation. Achieves 2.4-3.5× speedup in batch serving by generating multiple tokens per forward pass while maintaining distribution fidelity and regular batching, addressing the memory-bound bottleneck of autoregressive inference.

system.prefilter_rationale: Direct relevance to production LLM serving bottlenecks; K-Forcing addresses batch inference efficiency and latency—critical constraints in deployed RAG/agentic systems—with a practical distillation approach compatible with existing infrastructure.

items.title: Attention-Discounted Adaptive Sampler for Masked Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Introduces ADAS, a training-free attention-discounted reranking method for parallel masked diffusion language model decoding. Uses soft attention penalties to discount candidates attending to uncertain already-selected positions, improving subset construction while preserving existing samplers' stopping rules. Achieves 9-10% improvement on reasoning/code benchmarks with 3.1% overhead.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses production inference efficiency for LLMs through a training-free, modular reranking technique that improves parallel decoding quality with measurable speedup—actionable for optimizing LLM serving latency in constrained environments.

system.value_rationale: Relevant only if actively working with masked diffusion models (e.g., Genie, Muse-variants), which are rare in production RAG/agentic systems. items.title: Optimal Post-Training Quantization Scales and Where to Find Them
items.summary: PiSO algorithm computes optimal quantization scales for post-training quantization of LLMs by partitioning scale search space into intervals with closed-form minimizers. Extends to group-wise quantization and integrates with error correction methods like GPTQ, showing consistent perplexity improvements on Llama/Qwen models.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly applicable to production LLM deployment; PTQ is a standard compression technique for inference, and data-driven scale optimization addresses a practical bottleneck in quantization pipelines with demonstrated improvements on widely-used models.

items.title: AuRA: Internalizing Audio Understanding into LLMs as LoRA
items.summary: AuRA internalizes audio understanding into LLMs via LoRA by distilling speech representations from an ASR teacher into lightweight low-rank adapters in early LLM layers, eliminating the need for inference-time speech encoders while enabling efficient parallel end-to-end speech-language processing.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly applicable to production speech-to-LLM pipelines; LoRA-based adaptation is lightweight and deployable, addresses real latency/cost tradeoffs in cascaded vs. end-to-end architectures, and layer-wise distillation is an actionable engineering pattern for multimodal LLM systems.

items.title: TRACE: A Unified Rollout Budget Allocation Framework for Efficient Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: TRACE is a unified rollout budget allocation framework for agentic RL that allocates sampling budget to both prompt roots and intermediate prefixes most likely to yield mixed terminal rewards, enabling tree-structured rollouts with enhanced reward contrast within fixed computational budgets.

system.prefilter_rationale: Directly addresses production agentic RL optimization—rollout budget allocation, reward signal quality, and multi-turn reasoning efficiency are core pain points in shipping LLM agents; TRACE's tree-structured allocation and prefix-level informativeness modeling offer actionable patterns for improving sample efficiency in multi-step reasoning systems.

items.title: A Unifying Lens on Supervised Fine-Tuning Through Target Distribution Design
items.summary: Proposes a unifying framework for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) via target distribution design. items.title: Quantifying Subliminal Behavioral Transfer Ratios in Language Model Distillation

items.title: FlowBank: Query-Adaptive Agentic Workflows Optimization through Precompute-and-Reuse
items.summary: FlowBank optimizes LLM-based multi-agent workflows via portfolio-based selection. It generates diverse workflow candidates offline, compresses them into a compact bank, and routes queries adaptively at inference using bipartite graph matching to balance performance and cost.

items.title: When Probing Accuracy Saturates, Fragility Resolves: A Complementary Metric for LLM Pre-Training Analysis

items.title: APEX: Automated Prompt Engineering eXpert with Dynamic Data Selection
items.summary: APEX optimizes prompt engineering by dynamically selecting high-leverage training data rather than treating datasets as static. items.title: ISE: An Execution-Grounded Recipe for Multi-Turn OS-Agent Trajectories
items.summary: ISE is a three-stage execution-grounded synthesis paradigm for generating multi-turn OS-agent trajectories: intent construction via 4D structured sampling (Persona×Domain×Task×Complexity), multi-turn role-locked user simulation with state grounding, and live OS execution validation. items.title: Enhancing AI Interpretability and Safety through Localised Architectures
items.abstract: Recent advances in generative AI, especially powerful Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Reasoning Models (LRMs), raise concerns over the interpretability, safety and sustainability of these large and opaque AI models. The power of such architectures is derived not only from the scalability of deep neural networks, but also massively parallel hardware such as GPU clusters. The diffuse nature of deep neural networks gives them great function-approximation capability when provided with sufficient training data but imposes a cost in interpretability and computational efficiency. Observing that localised machine learning (ML) models tend to be more interpretable and computationally efficient than deep neural networks on small datasets, we reason by analogy that similar advantages may apply to specific localised hardware ML architectures. We argue that localised architectures with lower bandwidth but higher expressivity per node have the potential to be fundamentally more interpretable than deep neural networks running on GPU clusters while remaining competitive for smaller datasets. We then evaluate the suitability of various hardware ML paradigms for implementing such localised architectures and evaluate their per-node expressivity, energy efficiency and practical maturity of the technology required.

system.prefilter_rationale: While interpretability and safety are relevant to production AI systems, this paper's focus on novel hardware architectures and theoretical expressivity tradeoffs lacks direct applicability to current RAG, agentic, and document intelligence work—it requires hardware infrastructure changes outside typical engineering scope and doesn't address LLM-specific observability, evaluation, or operational concerns.

items.title: When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails: A Representation-Level Perspective
items.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) safety has often been evaluated at the behavior level, which provides limited evidence of internal robustness, as these evaluations target outputs rather than representation-level vulnerability under intervention. We formalize this discrepancy as the audit gap: the difference between behavioral safety and robustness under intervention. To study this gap, we construct dissociated models that preserve safe outward behavior while remaining vulnerable in the latent space. We introduce an intervention-based evaluation framework to test model robustness through soft interventions in parameter and latent spaces, including harmful fine-tuning and layer-wise latent perturbations. To formalize the evaluation, we propose the Latent Vulnerability Score (LVS) to measure how easily harmful behavior can be elicited by bounded latent perturbations. Using this evaluation framework, we show that behavioral safety metrics are insufficient measures of representation-level robustness across multiple safely and unsafely aligned state-of-the-art models. Notably, dissociated models show substantially elevated LVSs despite comparable refusal behavior under harmful intervention, with intermediate representations being the most sensitive to intervention. Our results suggest that behavioral safety evaluation alone provides an incomplete picture of model robustness, motivating representation-aware audits of latent vulnerability and observable behavior.

system.prefilter_rationale: While addressing LLM safety evaluation rigor, this paper is primarily theoretical/research-focused on understanding failure modes rather than providing actionable engineering patterns, production deployment strategies, or practical improvements to safety evaluation systems that practitioners can implement in RAG/agentic systems within a 6-month horizon.

items.title: OSMGraphCLIP: Learning Global Location Representations from OpenStreetMap Graphs
items.abstract: We present OSMGraphCLIP, a CLIP-style geospatial representation model that learns global location embeddings from freely available OpenStreetMap (OSM) data. OSMGraphCLIP represents geographic environments as heterogeneous graphs of typed OSM features, preserving the topological and semantic relationships among roads, buildings, land-use regions, and points of interest. A multi-scale graph encoder captures both fine-grained local structure and broader landscape composition, and supervises a spherical-harmonics location encoder through a contrastive alignment objective. We evaluate OSMGraphCLIP across a diverse suite of downstream geospatial regression and classification tasks spanning climate, ecology, socioeconomic indicators, public health, land cover, biodiversity, and wildfire forecasting, and show that structured OSM data alone supports strong global location representations across domains. OSMGraphCLIP matches or exceeds satellite-based baselines on the majority of benchmarks, with the most pronounced advantage on socioeconomic and public-health tasks, where OSM's explicit semantic annotation of the built environment encodes patterns of human activity that satellite pixels can only capture indirectly. On ecological and environmental tasks, the model remains closely competitive with imagery-based methods despite using no Earth observation data. Qualitative analysis confirms that the learned embeddings organize geographic space coherently, recovering biome boundaries, urban gradients, and tropical--temperate distinctions from map topology alone.

system.prefilter_rationale: While technically sound, this is a geospatial representation learning paper with no direct application to NLP, RAG systems, agentic workflows, document intelligence, or LLM-based production systems that constitute my core professional domain.

items.title: CLASP: Language-Driven Robot Skill Selection and Composition using Task-Parameterized Learning
items.abstract: Enabling robots to understand and execute tasks from natural language commands while maintaining data efficiency remains challenging. Foundation models such as vision-language-action (VLA) and vision-language models (VLMs) provide intuitive interaction channels but require extensive data; task-parameterized imitation learning achieves data efficiency but lacks natural language grounding. This work bridges this gap through a modular architecture combining task-parameterized kernelized movement primitives (TP-KMPs) with pretrained VLMs. During learning, skills are acquired from 2 to 5 kinesthetic demonstrations, and the VLM generates skill schemas describing each skill's parameters and preconditions. During execution, the VLM interprets commands to select skills, reason about parameter bindings, and create novel behaviors through covariance-weighted composition. When no skill or composition suffices, the system identifies capability gaps and requests targeted demonstrations, all without fine-tuning. Validation on a 7-DoF manipulator shows success rates of 73.3%-100% in scenarios requiring skill selection, composition, and active learning.

system.prefilter_rationale: Robotics skill composition and task-parameterized learning fall outside core NLP/RAG/agentic ML domains; while the VLM component is present, the paper is primarily a robotics control contribution without direct applicability to document intelligence or production NLP systems.

items.title: How Deep Are Deep GPs, Really? A Sharp Threshold and a Non-Gaussian Limit for Compositional GPs
items.abstract: Compositional priors describe the generic properties of layered functions in deep Bayesian models, where deep neural networks with random weights are a canonical example.In the wide-network limit, the prior is a Gaussian process with a depth-dependent kernel, and its behaviour as depth grows has been extensively studied through this kernel. Here, we study another case, where each layer itself is a vector valued Gaussian process, and our aim is similarly to understand the limiting behaviour of the prior as depth grows. Previous GP work has established that for the RBF kernel and a certain range of bandwidths $r$, the prior degenerates in the limit, converging to the set of constant functions -- which is not useful as a probabilistic model. In this paper we establish several new results. First, we identify a sharp bandwidth threshold $r_c(d) = Θ(\sqrt{d})$ above which the limit is degenerate, strengthening the earlier bounds. Second, and more importantly, we show that for $r$ below the threshold $r_c(d)$ the prior converges to a limit distribution $π_{\bar{Z}}$. We also prove that these distributions are non-degenerate and non-Gaussian, with non-vanishing dependence between coordinates. In contrast to the previously known degenerate regime, deep Gaussian process priors can therefore admit non-trivial limits. Empirically, we verify the threshold across a range of dimensions $d$, and demonstrate a complex multimodal behaviour of the limit distributions $π_{\bar{Z}}$ -- a regime that becomes increasingly narrow with $d$ and would be hard to identify without knowing the threshold.

system.prefilter_rationale: Pure theoretical analysis of GP limiting behavior with no demonstrated application to production RAG, agentic systems, document intelligence, or inference—outside evaluation scope for applied AI engineering.

items.title: Revisiting the shutdown problem
items.abstract: A key premise in leading arguments for existential risk from artificial intelligence is that malfunctioning artificial agents could not be easily shut down. This motivates the catastrophic shutdown problem of ensuring that agents can be shut down before they cause an existential catastrophe. A range of arguments and theorems are offered to suggest that solving the catastrophic shutdown problem is difficult, bolstering arguments for existential risk and motivating a search for solutions to the catastrophic shutdown problem. This paper argues for two conclusions. First, existing arguments do not establish the difficulty of solving the catastrophic shutdown problem. Second, concern for the catastrophic shutdown problem has led to technical solutions that impose a high safety tax on model performance.

system.prefilter_rationale: This is a theoretical safety argument paper focused on existential risk framing and philosophical critique of shutdown problem arguments, not engineering guidance for building production agentic systems, RAG pipelines, or LLM-based applications.

items.title: Chiaroscuro Attention: Spending Compute in the Dark
items.abstract: Standard transformers apply self-attention uniformly at every layer and token, regardless of whether the input requires dynamic cross-token interaction. We propose CHIAR-Former (Chiaroscuro Attention), a 4-layer hybrid transformer that routes each token to one of three operators - DCT spectral mixing, RBF kernel mixing, or full self-attention - based on per-token spectral entropy, a theoretically justified complexity signal. Through systematic ablation on WikiText-103, we discover routing collapse: the router consistently rejects RBF in favour of DCT and attention, revealing that spectral mixing and dynamic attention are complementary and sufficient. A purpose-designed DCT+Attention-only variant achieves Val PPL 36.54 on WikiText-103 - a 45% improvement over a full-attention baseline (PPL 66.62) at 62.5% fewer attention FLOPs. We extend evaluation to WikiText-2, IMDB sentiment classification, and synthetic ListOps operations, establishing a clear operating regime: CHIAR-Former excels on large-scale naturalistic text where token diversity supports spectral specialisation, while full attention retains an edge on small datasets and synthetic pattern-matching tasks. These findings - both the wins and the losses - together define when and why spectral routing earns its keep.

system.prefilter_rationale: While the paper addresses compute efficiency in transformers, it focuses on architectural novelty and theoretical spectral analysis rather than production-applicable patterns; the routing mechanism and spectral entropy signals lack demonstrated utility in real RAG, agentic, or document intelligence systems where practitioners operate.

items.title: Tensorizing Engram: Sharing Latents Across N-Gram Embeddings is Beneficial in LLMs
items.abstract: Modern language models represent text using discrete token-level embeddings, which forces recurring multi-token patterns to be learned implicitly across Transformer layers. Both Over-tokenized Transformers and Engram attempt to address this limitation by explicitly incorporating multi-token (n-gram) memories. However, they rely on separate hash tables for each n-gram order, which introduces hash collisions and prevents nested n-grams from sharing the underlying latent structures. To address these issues, we propose Tensorized Engram (TN-gram), a compact memory module that represents tensorized n-gram embeddings through shared factors in the Canonical Polyadic (CP) form. TN-gram learns shared token-position factors together with order-absorption vectors to encode the embeddings of different n-gram order. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that TN-gram matches or even outperforms Engram-style n-gram modules while requiring much fewer parameters.

system.prefilter_rationale: While the paper addresses embedding efficiency through tensor factorization, it focuses on a narrow architectural optimization (n-gram memory compression) rather than solving production RAG/agentic workflow problems, lacks clear latency/inference tradeoffs for serving, and the theoretical tensor decomposition contribution falls outside core applied NLP domains.

items.title: FiberTune: Preserving Action-Fiber Visual Residuals in Vision-Language-Action Fine-Tuning
